title: How early should you arrive at Dublin Airport?
author: Brogan
cover_image_alt: A passenger jet parked at an airport gate with an air bridge attached and baggage carts beside it
intro: Dublin Airport's own advice is two hours before a short-haul flight and three before long-haul, and more if you're dropping a bag or flying to the US. Here's how to work out the right time for your flight.
seo_title: Dublin Airport: arrive 2 or 3 hours before? (2026)
seo_description: 2 hours before short-haul and 3 before long-haul, says Dublin Airport, plus extra time for bags and US preclearance. Terminals, security hours and tips.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Short-haul:** 2 hours before
- **Long-haul:** 3 hours before
- **US flights:** 3 hours or more
- **Bags or a group:** add extra time

That's Dublin Airport's own guidance, checked in October 2026. Your airline sets the deadlines that actually matter, for check-in, bag drop and the boarding gate, and they're on your booking. Procedures change, so look at the airport's and your airline's current advice before you travel.

sections.heading: Which terminal?
sections.text:
Dublin has two terminals, and it's worth knowing which one you need before you set off, because they have separate security areas and separate drop-off points.

- **Terminal 1** is used by Ryanair and many other short-haul airlines.
- **Terminal 2** is Aer Lingus's home and has the US preclearance facility, so most flights to the United States leave from here.

Airlines do occasionally move, so check the terminal on your booking or in the airline's app the day before. The two terminals are a few minutes' walk apart, but getting dropped at the wrong one on a busy morning still costs you time.

According to the airport, security opens at 3am in Terminal 1 and 3.30am in Terminal 2 and stays open until the last departing flight. Turning up much earlier than that for a 6am flight won't get you through any faster.

sections.heading: Flying to the US: preclearance
sections.text:
Dublin is one of the few airports in Europe where you clear US immigration and customs before you fly. It means you land in the US as a domestic passenger and walk straight out, but it also means an extra set of checks in Dublin, after security and before the gate.

Watch out: preclearance has its own queue, and it closes before your flight does. Allow at least three hours for a US flight, and more in summer and around Christmas, when the queues are at their longest.

Make sure your ESTA or visa is approved well before you travel, and have your passport, boarding pass and the address you're staying at to hand.

sections.heading: How long to allow, worked out
sections.text:
Here's how the timings add up for a few common trips:

| Trip | Flight | Arrive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| City break, hand luggage only | Midday on a Tuesday | **About 2 hours** before |
| Sun holiday, bags to drop | 6.30am in July | **2½ hours** before |
| Long-haul to [Dubai](/destinations/dubai) | Any time | **3 hours** before |
| US flight, e.g. to [New York](/destinations/new-york) | Any time | **3 hours or more** before |

On a quiet midday flight, two hours leaves you plenty of time. July and August are Dublin's busiest months, and early mornings are the peak, when the first wave of holiday flights all leave at once. On top of that, bank holiday weekends and big match or concert weekends in Dublin make the queues longer.

sections.heading: Liquids and security
sections.text:
Dublin was one of the first big European airports to fit new CT-style scanners in both terminals. Since September 2025, according to the airport, liquids and gels can stay in your hand luggage, and the old 100ml limit doesn't apply to containers of up to two litres.

You still need to take off belts, jackets, hoodies and boots that come above the ankle, and empty your pockets into a tray.

Tip: the rules on your flight home are set by the airport you're flying from, and many still use the 100ml limit. Pack your liquids so they'll pass at both ends, or you might have to leave your sun cream behind on the way back.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.image_alt: A hand holding a phone showing a boarding pass in front of airport departure boards
sections.image_caption: Check in online and keep your boarding pass on your phone to skip the desks.
sections.text:
Dublin Airport has no train or tram, so it's road only:

- **By coach or bus:** Dublin Express and Aircoach run to the city centre, and several Dublin Bus routes stop at the airport. Early morning services are limited, so check the first one will get you there in time.
- **By car:** pre-booked parking is cheaper than turning up. The airport has had permission to charge for drop-off outside the terminals, so check the current arrangements, and the free drop-off point at the long-term car park, before you go.
- **By taxi:** allow extra time for the M50 and the Port Tunnel at rush hour.

If you're relying on the first coach of the day for an early flight, it's often worth booking a taxi instead.

sections.heading: Five ways to make the airport easier
sections.text:
- **Check in online** as soon as it opens, and keep your boarding pass on your phone.
- **Travel with hand luggage only** if you can, so you can skip bag drop.
- **Check your terminal** the day before.
- **Use Fast Track** on a busy morning: Dublin sells it for both terminals, for a fee.
- **Head to the gate early:** some gates are a long walk from security, and they close before the published departure time.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Dublin?
sections.text:
Dublin has direct flights almost everywhere, from short hops to [Lisbon](/destinations/lisbon) and [Barcelona](/destinations/barcelona) to winter sun in [Lanzarote](/destinations/lanzarote) and long-haul to [New York](/destinations/new-york). The [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) and [beach holidays](/destinations/beach-holidays) pages are good places to start.

If you're stuck choosing as a family or group, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put everyone's ideas into a draw and let it decide.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Dublin Airport for a Ryanair flight?
faqs.answer: Dublin Airport advises two hours before a short-haul flight, and more if you're dropping a bag or travelling in a group. Ryanair flies from Terminal 1, and its bag drop closes well before departure, so check the time on your booking.

faqs.question: Is 2 hours enough at Dublin Airport?
faqs.answer: For a short-haul flight with hand luggage only, usually yes. Allow longer in July and August, on early mornings and on bank holiday weekends, and allow at least three hours for a US flight.

faqs.question: How early should I arrive at Dublin Airport for a US flight?
faqs.answer: At least three hours. You go through US preclearance in Terminal 2 as well as normal security, and the preclearance queue closes before the flight does.

faqs.question: What time does security open at Dublin Airport?
faqs.answer: According to the airport, security opens at 3am in Terminal 1 and 3.30am in Terminal 2, and stays open until the last flight.

faqs.question: Can you take liquids through security at Dublin Airport?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since September 2025, according to the airport, liquids in containers of up to two litres can stay in your hand luggage. The airport you fly home from may still use the 100ml limit.
